title: Paloma and the Lantern
premise: Rosalind Brightwater, a pearl diver's daughter indentured to the Meridian Trading Company, has survived by being unremarkable — carrying ledgers, cargo, and secrets through a colonial port city sliding toward war. When a wounded stranger arrives bearing letters in the handwriting of her father, officially drowned twelve years ago, she is pulled into a conspiracy to falsify the company's wartime losses and erase the divers who died in its service. As armistice negotiations approach, Rosalind must choose between the safety of invisibility and putting the truth on record before the victors' historians write it away, discovering along the way that love and duty are not opposites but rival claims on the same heart. She ends by testifying at the commission hearings, losing her indenture and nearly her life, but winning back her name — and her father, alive, broken, and finally hers.
about_author: Ulyana Vasquez is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing trading-company ledgers from the late colonial era. Her fiction excavates the lives of laborers whose names appear only in margins and margin notes.

chapters.title: What the Water Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. In the port of Saltmere, Rosalind dives for pearls under Meridian Company contract, measuring her life in what can be carried when orders come. A routine inventory day establishes her world: the ledgers, the overseers, the memory of her drowned father. Emotional beat: quiet resignation masking grief.

chapters.title: The Weight of Paper
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Summoned to the counting house, she copies shipping manifests and glimpses an entry marked 'losses — divers, unserviceable.' Her supervisor warns her to forget it. That night she practices her father's old diving breaths in the shallows. Emotional beat: first crack in her practiced invisibility.

chapters.title: A Stranger with Wet Boots
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. A wounded man named Elias Corvane collapses near the drying racks, carrying satchels of letters — one unmistakably in her father Tomas Brightwater's handwriting, dated three years after his reported drowning. She hides him before the harbor patrol arrives. Emotional beat: shock hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Handwriting of the Dead
chapters.summary: POV Elias. Elias, a former company clerk turned investigator, explains he traced falsified loss records across three ports; Tomas may be alive, held where he can't testify. Rosalind doesn't trust him, but the handwriting is proof against doubt. Emotional beat: wary alliance formed over shared evidence.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Second Spine
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. The pair discover the company keeps two sets of books: public losses modest, private ones catastrophic, including deliberate over-diving that killed dozens. Rosalind recognizes names of women she grew up with. Emotional beat: personal grief becomes political fury.

chapters.title: Orders Come at Dawn
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. The company announces wartime requisition: all divers conscripted to salvage a sunken munitions ship. Rosalind must report or flee and forfeit everything. She chooses to go, taking Elias's copied pages sewn into her diving coat. Emotional beat: duty as a cage she walks into willingly.

chapters.title: The Salvage Grounds
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. On the wreck, conditions are lethal; the foreman pushes depth records to meet quotas. Rosalind saves a young diver, Nettie, from a collapse, earning quiet loyalty among the crew. Emotional beat: solidarity discovered in shared danger.

chapters.title: Letters Under Salt
chapters.summary: POV Elias. Elias works the port archives by day, dodging a company fixer named Hargrave who suspects him. He finds the armistice commission will accept testimony only until signing — six weeks. Emotional beat: the clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: The Foreman's Price
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. The foreman offers Rosalind exemption from deep dives if she reports 'agitators' among the crew. She refuses, and he marks her for the worst shifts. Nettie begins helping her smuggle messages to Elias. Emotional beat: corruption shown as small, transactional, ordinary.

chapters.title: Hargrave Comes Aboard
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Hargrave inspects the salvage operation, hunting Elias. Rosalind misdirects him at real risk, then realizes he recognized her father's name on a manifest. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into cunning.

chapters.title: What My Mother Carried
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Visiting her mother's grave, Rosalind recalls how her mother died waiting for a husband declared dead, and how Rosalind swore never to hope. Elias joins her; something unspoken settles between them. Emotional beat: grief and love entangling against her will.

chapters.title: The Drowned Man's Address
chapters.summary: POV Elias. Decoding a letter's postal marks, they locate the island holding house where inconvenient witnesses like Tomas are kept. It lies inside the naval exclusion zone. Emotional beat: hope arriving disguised as an impossible plan.

chapters.title: Nettie's Choice
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Nettie discovers the smuggling and must decide whether to betray Rosalind for safety. Instead she reveals her own sister was listed as an 'unserviceable loss.' The crew quietly aligns behind them. Emotional beat: the conspiracy grows roots among the powerless.

chapters.title: Storm Season
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. A storm wrecks the salvage schedule; the company blames diver sabotage and arrests two crewmen. Rosalind realizes the arrests are theater to justify harsher control before the armistice silences everything. Emotional beat: dread of the closing window.

chapters.title: The Long Row Out
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind and Elias alternating. Under cover of storm debris, Rosalind, Elias, and Nettie row to the holding island. They find Tomas alive but half-broken, refusing to leave until his testimony is written down properly. Emotional beat: reunion shadowed by damage.

chapters.title: A Father Made of Paper
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Tomas, ill and lucid only in intervals, dictates his account while Rosalind transcribes — the same ledgers she once copied now corrected by his voice. Father and daughter negotiate twelve lost years between sentences. Emotional beat: reconciliation without easy forgiveness.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Counting House
chapters.summary: POV Elias. Hargrave captures Nettie during a supply run and offers trade: Elias's evidence for the girl. Elias considers surrendering the documents; Rosalind refuses to let truth be bartered. They attempt an exchange that goes wrong. Emotional beat: the cost of principle made flesh.

chapters.title: Fire on the Water
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Escaping the botched exchange, they lose most of the copied evidence to fire but keep Tomas's original testimony hidden in Rosalind's diving coat. Nettie is freed in the chaos; Elias is wounded shielding Rosalind. Emotional beat: despair, then fierce clarity about what matters.

chapters.title: The Commission Sits
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Armistice week: the commission convenes in Saltmere's customs hall, crowded with company lawyers. Rosalind walks in openly for the first time in her life, Tomas on her arm, and requests to be heard. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into standing.

chapters.title: On the Record
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Climax. Rosalind testifies, reading Tomas's account aloud as he confirms each line; Hargrave attempts to discredit her as an indentured liar, but Nettie and surviving divers corroborate. The commission accepts the testimony into the record hours before signing. Emotional beat: triumph earned at full price.

chapters.title: What Cannot Be Carried
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Aftermath: the company's officers face inquiry, Hargrave flees, and Rosalind's indenture is voided. But the victory is partial — many names stay unrecovered, and Elias receives orders elsewhere. They part at the harbor without promises, only honesty. Emotional beat: bittersweet release.

chapters.title: Paloma and the Lantern
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind, epilogue. A year later, Rosalind runs a small diving cooperative with Nettie, teaching girls to read water and ledger alike. Tomas tends the lamp above the harbor. Each night she lights it for the names on the restored record. Emotional beat: peace as an act of remembrance, not forgetting.
